notes: Account summary: large global payments provider exploring Redwood Dedicated + Private for inference workloads supporting fraud, support chat, and authorization flow reranking.
Primary ask: guaranteed throughput for peak windows (APAC morning, NA evening) + clear latency SLOs for synchronous auth paths.
"On call" quote from CTO: 'we cannot have tail latency spikes during peak settlement windows; plan must include cross-region failover capacity.'
Deployment constraints: must support VPC-only control plane, KMS in customer-managed HSM, and EU data residency for EU customers. Air-gapped option for some regulated partners (possible later phase).
Cost sensitivity: high; finance wants clear ARR bands for reserved GPU commitments vs. burst/spot. Target ROI horizon: 12 months after deployment.
Technical preference: stay on open large models (7B–34B) with quantized variants; want Redwood to recommend quantization/batching profiles per workload.
Throughput targets (provided by client):
- Chat agents: sustained 1,200 qps across global routes during peak (average request size ~120 tokens).
- Embeddings: 5k qps batchable offline; nearline for fraud feature stores with <300ms p95 per request when served via dedicated endpoints.
- Reranking: synchronous path for authorization, target p95 inference latency <250ms end-to-end (model compute + network),
"Latency policy" internal note: measure at token-level and end-to-end; need Redwood to provide billing/monitoring hooks tied to SLOs.
Reserved GPU planning preferences:
- Multi-region topology: active-active in NA + EU with APAC as warm standby. Prefer AZ-spread in each region with affinity routing to nearest regional pool.
- Failover headroom: want 30% spare capacity per region for intra-region AZ failover, plus an additional 25% cross-region capacity reserved for full-region failover scenarios.
- Warm pool strategy: maintain a small standing warm-pool (10–15% of baseline) for cold-start sensitive endpoints (authorization reranking).
- Canary and rollout: phased canary on 1 node per AZ, auto-scale disabled for critical routes; use burst capacity for non-critical chat if dedicated pool saturated.
SLA negotiation items raised by legal/ops:
- Define measurable throughput guarantee (requests/sec at p95) per reserved GPU unit and per route
- Credits for SLO misses tied to regional outages and failovers, not for planned maintenance
- Clear RTO/RPO expectations for cross-region failover and stateful cache warm-up time (KV cache warming for model keys).
Evaluation POC specifics so far:
- 2-week sustained soak in NA: 100 GPUs (A100 equivalent) reserved, config captured in drive playbook
- Short APAC warm-standby test: burst to APAC pool during NA simulated outage, measured cold-start penalty 2.8s to first token (acceptable for chat but not for reranking).
"Security review" progress: completed SOC2 questionnaire, pending architecture diagrams for HSM integration (SEC-1911).
Notes from SE call 2026-03-02 (Liam): prioritized action items - provide a regional sizing spreadsheet, warm-headroom cost scenarios, proposed SLA addendum language.
Finance note (emailed 2026-02-26): wants 3 pricing options: conservative (low headroom), recommended (30% regional + 25% cross-region), and aggressive (50% headroom for top-critical routes).
Sales suggestion: propose 12-month reserved baseline with 6-month review to adjust reserved counts based on observed 95th percentile and model mix changes.
Obvious risk: model architecture changes (moving to larger model family) can increase token cost and reduce effective qps per GPU — include a model-change clause in contract.

requirements_summary: Primary workloads: low-latency reranking for authorization (p95 <250ms), chat agents with high concurrency, embeddings backfill and nearline serving
Latency SLO: p50 <80ms for model compute on dedicated pool; p95 end-to-end <250ms for reranking routes (network included)
Throughput guarantee: baseline regional qps commitments + 30% intra-region headroom for AZ failover; additional 25% reserved cross-region for full-region failover
Failure modes: AZ outage -> traffic shifted within region (headroom requirement). Region outage -> failover to secondary region within 60–120s with degraded latency tolerances for non-critical paths
Warm-headroom: maintain 10–15% warm pool to mitigate cold-start for critical synchronous endpoints
Observability: token-level tracing, per-route latency & cost breakdown, and alerts when utilization >70% of reserved capacity
Operational: quarterly capacity review, 6-month reserved adjustment window, canary rollouts required for model version changes
